head: Acute
Chronic
visuals.text: Example: farmer's lung from fungal spores; confirm with serum precipitins.

visual.title: Chest X-ray
visual.caption: Bilateral reticular shadowing and honeycombing, basal and peripheral; HRCT confirms the UIP pattern.

children.label: Mechanism
items: Direct cytotoxic injury to alveolar cells

visuals.title: Organs affected
visuals.text: Lung fibrosis eventually strains the right side of the heart.

glossary.Interstitial lung fibrosis: Scarring of the tissue between the alveoli that stiffens the lungs.
glossary.Gas exchange: Movement of oxygen into, and carbon dioxide out of, the blood in the alveoli.
glossary.Idiopathic interstitial pneumonia: A group of lung-scarring or inflammatory diseases of unknown cause; IPF is the main one.
glossary.CTD: Connective tissue disease, such as rheumatoid arthritis, SLE or scleroderma.
glossary.Sarcoidosis: Multisystem disease with non-caseating granulomas, often in the lungs and lymph nodes.
glossary.Prognosis: The likely course and outcome of a disease.
glossary.Cyanosis: Blue tinge to skin or lips from low blood oxygen.
glossary.Exertional dyspnoea: Breathlessness brought on by physical activity.
glossary.End-inspiratory: Occurring at the end of breathing in.
glossary.Bibasal: At the bases of both lungs.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: Autoimmune disease of the joints that can also cause lung fibrosis.
glossary.SLE: Systemic lupus erythematosus: a multisystem autoimmune disease.
glossary.Scleroderma: Autoimmune disease causing hardening of skin and sometimes internal organs, including lungs.
glossary.Coal worker's pneumoconiosis: Lung scarring from inhaled coal dust.
glossary.Histiocytosis: A rare disorder where histiocytes (immune cells) build up and damage tissues, including lung.
glossary.Airspace opacification: Areas of white on X-ray where air spaces are filled with fluid or cells.
glossary.Aspergillus: A common mould whose spores can trigger allergic and hypersensitivity lung disease.
glossary.Fungal spores: Tiny reproductive particles released by moulds, easily inhaled.
glossary.Parenchyma: The functional tissue of an organ; in the lung, the alveoli and their walls.
glossary.Cystic airspaces: Abnormal round air-filled spaces with walls.
glossary.Bronchoscopy: Passing a camera down the airways to look inside and take samples.
glossary.Reticulonodular shadowing: A net-like pattern with small nodules on chest X-ray, seen in interstitial disease.
glossary.Vital capacity: The most air that can be breathed out after a full breath in.
glossary.Autoimmune screen: Blood tests for antibodies that suggest an autoimmune disease.
glossary.Echocardiogram: Ultrasound scan of the heart showing structure and function.
glossary.Right heart strain: The right ventricle under excess pressure load, often from pulmonary hypertension.
glossary.Disease-modifying: A treatment that changes the course of the disease, not just symptoms.
glossary.N-acetylcysteine: An antioxidant drug sometimes used in IPF; better known as the paracetamol overdose antidote.
glossary.Lung transplantation: Surgical replacement of one or both diseased lungs with donor lungs.
glossary.Opiates: Morphine-like drugs; low doses ease breathlessness in end-stage lung disease.
glossary.Benzodiazepines: Sedative drugs such as lorazepam; can ease anxiety from breathlessness.
glossary.Palliative care: Care focused on comfort and quality of life when cure is not possible.
glossary.Hypoxia: Low oxygen levels in the tissues.
glossary.Hypoxaemia: Low oxygen level in the blood.
glossary.Alveolar epithelial cells: The thin cells lining the air sacs, where gas exchange takes place.
glossary.Aberrant wound healing: Faulty repair after injury that lays down too much scar tissue.
glossary.Fibroblast: A cell that makes collagen and other scar tissue proteins.
glossary.Collagen: The main structural protein of connective and scar tissue.
glossary.ECM: Extracellular matrix: the protein scaffold between cells, including collagen.
glossary.Diffusion distance: How far gases must travel between alveolar air and blood.
glossary.Cytotoxic: Toxic to cells, directly damaging or killing them.
glossary.Pulmonary vascular remodelling: Thickening and narrowing of the lung blood vessel walls.
glossary.Right heart failure: The right ventricle fails to pump blood through the lungs, causing fluid back-up.
